methods.name: Structured intake and triage
methods.summary: Turn the reported symptom into a scoped case, a data-protection decision and a measurable next test.
methods.when: Use at the beginning of a job or when ownership changes.
methods.proof: Exact failure, affected scope, protected data and next action are recorded.

methods.name: Layered malware assessment
methods.summary: Combine an updated primary product, purposeful second-opinion checks and persistence review.
methods.when: Use for suspected local malware when active spread has been addressed.
methods.proof: Detections, coverage, account exposure and the original user task have a documented outcome.

methods.name: Incident containment
methods.summary: Limit spread while preserving the evidence and coordination needed for recovery.
methods.when: Use for active encryption, wider compromise or credible spreading-threat evidence.
methods.proof: Isolation, incident ownership, affected scope and controlled reconnection criteria are recorded.

methods.name: Evidence-led performance diagnosis
methods.summary: Tie a repeatable slow task to a measured resource or dependency before changing settings.
methods.when: Use for slowness, freezes or hitching with an observable workload.
methods.proof: The same workload improves and required applications, protection and devices still work.

methods.name: Windows image and system-file repair
methods.summary: Use the supported servicing path for verified component or protected-system-file corruption.
methods.when: Use after storage health and the intended online or offline installation are established.
methods.proof: Servicing results and the originally failing function both pass after restart.

methods.name: Controlled update repair
methods.summary: Identify the failed update and its actual blocker before resetting or replacing components.
methods.when: Use when an update fails repeatedly or cannot complete its restart phase.
methods.proof: Update history, installed build and the affected workload agree.

methods.name: Windows startup recovery
methods.summary: Follow the observed boot stage and recover the correct installation through supported options.
methods.when: Use when the operating system will not start normally.
methods.proof: The intended installation boots repeatedly with data, encryption and applications intact.

methods.name: Image-first recovery
methods.summary: Preserve readable data from failing media before attempting repairs on the source.
methods.when: Use for repeated I/O errors, disappearing drives or credible physical-failure evidence.
methods.proof: Source identity, image, mapfile, unreadable regions and recovered-file usability are recorded.

methods.name: Verified disk migration
methods.summary: Move a healthy system or its data while retaining a recoverable original.
methods.when: Use when replacing a healthy disk or moving to a new workstation.
methods.proof: The destination boots or opens the required data independently and the source remains available through acceptance.

methods.name: Backup and restore proof
methods.summary: Prove recovery by restoring representative data to a separate destination.
methods.when: Use before relying on a backup and after a material backup configuration change.
methods.proof: Restored data opens with correct permissions and recorded recovery dependencies.

methods.name: Layered network diagnosis
methods.summary: Separate physical link, addressing, name resolution, transport and application failures.
methods.when: Use when connectivity fails or behaves differently across devices or services.
methods.proof: The original application works through the intended path and adjacent services remain healthy.

methods.name: Dependency-ordered outage recovery
methods.summary: Restore foundational services before the systems that depend on them.
methods.when: Use after an office power failure or a multi-service interruption.
methods.proof: A client workstation completes the real business workflow and degraded dependencies have owners.

methods.name: Attended remote support
methods.summary: Reach the intended device with the person present and close temporary access when finished.
methods.when: Use for an agreed one-time support session.
methods.proof: Device identity, session outcome and access closure are documented.

methods.name: Directory trust diagnosis
methods.summary: Check identity, connectivity and the member-machine secure channel before a scoped repair.
methods.when: Use for a domain trust error on a member workstation.
methods.proof: Fresh sign-in and required resources work with a unique active computer identity.

methods.name: Mail-flow isolation
methods.summary: Distinguish service/account delivery failures from a local mail-client problem.
methods.when: Use when sending, receiving or a specific mailbox workflow fails.
methods.proof: A message arrives, a reply returns and required archives or shared-mailbox behavior still work.

methods.name: Print-path isolation
methods.summary: Separate printer hardware, network reachability, queue, driver and application output.
methods.when: Use when printing fails or output is wrong.
methods.proof: Internal and application test pages pass without breaking other users or queues.

methods.name: Crash and hardware isolation
methods.summary: Correlate the failure with evidence and test one plausible hardware or software cause.
methods.when: Use for stop errors, unexpected restarts, overheating or reproducible instability.
methods.proof: The original failure scenario and the relevant diagnostics have recorded outcomes.

methods.name: Baseline workstation deployment
methods.summary: Prepare a workstation around the employee's required tasks and a verified recovery route.
methods.when: Use for a new or replacement computer.
methods.proof: The employee completes agreed tasks and recovery, backup and remote-support arrangements are verified.

methods.name: Verified client handoff
methods.summary: Close the job with observed proof, clear changes and explicit remaining work.
methods.when: Use after repair or when responsibility moves to another technician.
methods.proof: The user accepts the result or the remaining-work plan and the next action is unambiguous.

methods.name: Boot-media preparation
methods.summary: Acquire, verify, write and boot-test the media intended for the job.
methods.when: Use before relying on a new image or refreshed technician USB.
methods.proof: Image identity, checksum result, intended USB and actual boot evidence are recorded separately.

methods.name: Redacted AI-assisted triage
methods.summary: Use an assistant to reason about minimal sanitized evidence, then independently verify its proposal.
methods.when: Use when explaining a log or comparing possible next tests.
methods.proof: No unnecessary secrets were shared and executed actions match verified documentation and observed evidence.

methods.name: Evidence-led preventive maintenance
methods.summary: Review actual protection, updates, recovery and hardware needs before changing the workstation.
methods.when: Use for a planned maintenance visit.
methods.proof: The normal workload passes and each failed or deferred item has an owner and next action.

methods.name: Scope isolation
methods.summary: Vary the user, device, application or service boundary to locate the smallest failing scope.
methods.when: Use when the symptom is vague or reported as affecting everything.
methods.proof: A failing and a working comparison establish the next investigation boundary.

methods.name: Known-good comparison
methods.summary: Compare with a verified working device, account, cable or configuration under matching conditions.
methods.when: Use when an interchangeable component can distinguish likely causes.
methods.proof: The compared conditions and the result for both paths are recorded.

methods.name: Single-change experiment
methods.summary: Make one reversible change that tests a stated hypothesis.
methods.when: Use when several explanations could fit the current evidence.
methods.proof: The predicted result, actual result and rollback are recorded before another variable changes.

methods.name: Reproducible baseline
methods.summary: Record the failing task, input, configuration and measurement before changing the system.
methods.when: Use before claiming a repair or performance improvement.
methods.proof: Another technician can repeat the same workload and compare equivalent observations.

methods.name: Rollback rehearsal
methods.summary: Confirm how to restore the previous working configuration before a disruptive change.
methods.when: Use for upgrades, migrations and other changes that can interrupt service.
methods.proof: The retained source, access method and restoration steps are usable.

methods.name: Restore verification
methods.summary: Recover representative files to a separate target and open them in their real application.
methods.when: Use when a backup report is the only existing assurance.
methods.proof: Content, permissions, application usability and recovery time are recorded.

methods.name: Source and destination verification
methods.summary: Identify both storage endpoints by stable device details and intended read/write direction.
methods.when: Use before imaging, cloning, writing boot media or recovering files.
methods.proof: The source is preserved and the intended destination is the one that changed.

methods.name: BitLocker recovery readiness
methods.summary: Locate the correct recovery material and match the key identifier before a change that can affect startup.
methods.when: Use before boot, firmware, storage or recovery changes on an encrypted device.
methods.proof: The authorized recovery path is reachable from another device and the matching key reference is recorded privately.

methods.name: Publisher and checksum verification
methods.summary: Check the official distribution route, expected publisher signature and provided cryptographic digest.
methods.when: Use before introducing an installer, executable or boot image into the technician kit.
methods.proof: The exact file, publisher/check result, expected digest and source are recorded; a mismatch remains unresolved.

methods.name: Cold and warm comparison
methods.summary: Measure the same workload with documented initial and repeated-run conditions.
methods.when: Use when caches or initialization could explain a claimed speed improvement.
methods.proof: Input and configuration match and both first-run and repeated-run outcomes are retained.

methods.name: Timestamp correlation
methods.summary: Align the symptom time with relevant logs and recent changes without equating correlation to cause.
methods.when: Use for intermittent crashes, update failures or incidents.
methods.proof: Timezones, clock uncertainty and the supporting sequence are recorded.

methods.name: Read-only evidence collection
methods.summary: Collect the smallest useful observation before applying a change to the target.
methods.when: Use when the next action could overwrite diagnostic or recovery evidence.
methods.proof: Original observations remain available and any gaps in coverage are visible.

methods.name: Least-privilege remote access
methods.summary: Limit a support session or persistent agent to the identities, devices and duration actually needed.
methods.when: Use when selecting a remote-support access model.
methods.proof: Access ownership, scope, duration and removal or continuing-management decision are documented.

methods.name: DNS-versus-connectivity isolation
methods.summary: Test name resolution separately from address reachability and the application connection.
methods.when: Use when an address works but a name fails, or different resolvers give different results.
methods.proof: The failing layer is identified without replacing organization-specific DNS blindly.

methods.name: Application-profile isolation
methods.summary: Compare the affected application configuration with a clean or known-working profile while retaining the original.
methods.when: Use after service/account checks point toward local application state.
methods.proof: Required local data is preserved and the same task is compared in both profiles.

methods.name: Post-change acceptance
methods.summary: Repeat the original workflow and relevant neighboring functions after a change.
methods.when: Use before calling a repair complete or promoting a new kit component.
methods.proof: Observed results meet the agreed success criteria and remaining issues have owners.

methods.name: Manual freshness review
methods.summary: Read the official release and compatibility evidence before changing a catalog review date or installing an update.
methods.when: Use when a checker reports a new release, changed URL or outdated review.
methods.proof: Release identity, applicable changes, compatibility and a dated editorial decision are recorded.

methods.name: Stable-release promotion
methods.summary: Move a candidate into routine use only after its defined job and recovery path are exercised.
methods.when: Use when evaluating a new tool version or a research candidate.
methods.proof: Equivalent work, relevant behavior, resource cost and rollback evidence support the promotion.

methods.name: Remote capability preflight
methods.summary: Match the session to the job and prove the required control, file, privilege and reconnect paths before changing the endpoint.
methods.when: Before choosing or starting a one-time or managed support connection.
methods.proof: Both platforms, user presence, permissions, transfer route and reconnect plan are recorded and the required capabilities are exercised.

methods.name: Temporary access revocation
methods.summary: Close every case-specific session and remove temporary access while preserving explicitly authorized managed access.
methods.when: At the end of remote work or when ownership and scope change.
methods.proof: Session end, closed channels and removed credentials/enrollments are recorded, or continuing access has a named owner and review date.

methods.name: Scan coverage reconciliation
methods.summary: Report findings separately from scope, inaccessible regions, cancellation and completion.
methods.when: After each malware scan and before a cleanup or escalation decision.
methods.proof: The case has scan mode, version, scope, completion, exclusions or errors, findings and disposition with the product report.

methods.name: Clean rebuild acceptance
methods.summary: Carry the case safely from preserved evidence and data to a trusted installation and demonstrated customer task.
methods.when: When the trusted endpoint baseline cannot be established or the incident owner requires rebuilding.
methods.proof: Pre-wipe target and data decisions, media provenance, patch/protection state, restore checks, account-response ownership and customer-task evidence are recorded.

methods.name: Image and mapfile reconciliation
methods.summary: Bind an acquired image to its device identities, rescue-domain coverage, persistent mapfile and stopped-checkpoint checksum.
methods.when: At an imaging checkpoint and before filesystem repair or extraction from a working copy.
methods.proof: Saved mapfile states, remaining unreadable ranges, matching image/mapfile checkpoint and healthy-storage copy checks are recorded separately from file usability.
